news.headline: Democratic campaign in Alaska accused of recruiting namesake candidate to split vote
news.summary: A New York Times investigation reported that staff from Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola’s campaign helped recruit a second candidate named Dan Sullivan to run in the Alaska U.S. Senate race. The effort was intended to draw votes away from incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan. The alleged ballot‑stacking has prompted a Department of Justice inquiry and political controversy. The case highlights concerns about election tactics in a closely watched race.

news.headline: Conservative activists charged with unlawful voting and identity theft in Minnesota
news.summary: Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty announced felony charges against James O'Keefe and Cam Higby. The charges allege they impersonated registered voters and used disguises, including Muslim attire, to vote in the August primary. Prosecutors say the stunt was intended to highlight perceived weaknesses in Minnesota’s voter‑vouching system. The case raises questions about election security and the legality of undercover political activism.

news.headline: Federal Reserve Holds Interest Rates Steady Ahead of Midterm Elections
news.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to keep the federal funds rate target at 3.75%‑4.0% on Wednesday. Two members, Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack, dissented, arguing for a hike. The decision comes as inflation remains elevated and the nation approaches the midterm elections. Markets had largely expected the hold, but the timing raises political and economic interest.

news.headline: Labor leader Dolores Huerta, co‑founder of United Farm Workers, dies at 96
news.summary: Dolores Huerta, a longtime labor organizer and civil‑rights activist who co‑founded the United Farm Workers with Cesar Chavez, died on Wednesday at age 96. She was a prominent figure in the farm‑worker movement and helped advance rights for Latino agricultural workers. Her death marks the loss of a key architect of modern labor activism and has prompted reflection on her legacy.

news.headline: At least 64 dead in high‑speed train collision in central Spain
news.summary: Two high‑speed passenger trains on the Madrid‑Seville line collided on Wednesday morning, killing at least 64 people and injuring dozens. The crash involved the state‑owned operator Renfe and private operator Iryo. Spain’s transport minister cited a failed control system as a possible cause. The disaster comes days before a national election, raising concerns about public safety and political accountability.

news.headline: Defeated Brazilian candidate Flávio Bolsonaro lands in Miami after fleeing Brazil
news.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost Brazil’s presidential election, departed the country with his family and arrived in Miami. He left after a court ordered him to surrender his passports. His arrival ends weeks of speculation about his whereabouts and highlights tensions between the new administration and the former president’s allies.

news.headline: Alaska GOP Senator Lisa Murkowski Endorses Democrat for Governor
news.summary: Republican Senator Lisa Murkowski announced she will back Democrat Jonathan Kreiss‑Tomkins in the Alaska gubernatorial race. The endorsement crosses party lines ahead of the 2024 midterm elections. It highlights intra‑party tensions and could influence the governor’s contest and Republican unity in Alaska.

news.headline: Federal Judge Alvin Hellerstein, overseeing Maduro case, dies at 92
news.summary: U.S. District Judge Alvin Hellerstein, a 92‑year‑old jurist appointed by President Bill Clinton, died of natural causes. He had been presiding over the criminal prosecution of deposed Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro. Hellerstein also handled several high‑profile cases, including matters involving former President Donald Trump. His death leaves the Maduro case without its assigned judge, prompting a reassignment process.

news.headline: Trump and Talarico hold separate rallies in Lubbock as Texas Senate race heats up
news.summary: Republican former president Donald Trump and Democratic state representative James Talarico held separate rallies in Lubbock, Texas on Tuesday. Trump’s appearances were part of his effort to back incumbent Attorney General Ken Paxton in his bid for the U.S. Senate seat. Talarico’s rally was aimed at promoting his own campaign for the same Senate seat. The dueling events highlight the competitiveness of the Texas Senate race.

news.headline: Hasan Piker sues commentator Scott Jennings for $72.5M defamation claim
news.summary: Progressive Twitch streamer Hasan Piker filed a federal defamation lawsuit against conservative commentator Scott Jennings, alleging Jennings falsely said Piker supported lynching Black people. The suit seeks $72.5 million in damages. The case centers on a clip aired on Jennings' show that Piker says was manipulated. The outcome could affect how political commentary is litigated.
